problem: Urban robot navigation foundation models map monocular RGB directly to actions and skip mid-level vision (depth, tracking), which needs huge pixel-to-action supervision and struggles in dynamic scenes because monocular views have depth-scale ambiguity.
motivation: Dynamic, unstructured urban settings need precise geometric and motion understanding, and pixel-to-action data is expensive to collect. Modern mid-level vision models (stereo depth, dense tracking) already provide reliable geometry and motion, so using them explicitly could greatly improve data efficiency.
key_idea: Augment a navigation foundation model with stereo inputs and explicit mid-level vision (depth estimation and dense pixel tracking), and train it on a new large stereo navigation dataset auto-annotated from Internet stereo videos.
insight: Per the abstract, explicit mid-level vision lets the model match state-of-the-art performance with only 1.5% of the training data and exceed it with full data. Stereo input also beats monocular input, which suggests that resolving depth-scale ambiguity and supplying explicit geometry and motion cues reduces reliance on implicit emergence from large-scale supervision. Only the abstract was available, so ablation details are unknown.
method: StereoWalker: navigation foundation model that takes stereo image input instead of monocular input and outputs control actions.
Mid-level vision integration: explicit depth estimation and dense pixel tracking features feed the policy to give geometric and motion structure in dynamic scenes.
Stereo navigation dataset: large dataset curated from Internet stereo videos with automatic action annotation, used for training and released for future research.

setting.backbone: StereoWalker (stereo NFM with mid-level vision models for depth and tracking); details not given in the abstract
setting.training_data: Curated large stereo navigation dataset from Internet stereo videos with automatic action labels (scale not given in the abstract); also tested with 1.5% of the training data
setting.observation: stereo RGB images (plus derived depth and dense pixel tracks)
setting.action_space: control actions (details not given in the abstract)

results: StereoWalker reaches performance comparable to the state-of-the-art using only 1.5% of the training data and surpasses the state-of-the-art with the full data. Stereo input yields higher navigation performance than monocular input. No specific numbers are given in the abstract.
limitations: Only the abstract was available, so benchmarks, metrics and ablations could not be checked.
Depends on the quality of external depth and tracking models and on automatically annotated actions from Internet videos.
builds_on: mid-level vision models (depth estimation, dense pixel tracking)
compares_to: state-of-the-art monocular urban navigation foundation models
